sourceEvidence.label: Supplied Concept NACK and Bails master source snapshot

assessment.summary: The evidence supports narrowing CipherStick's claims and runtime to a testable, authenticated support boundary; it does not support rejecting all automation or Bash categorically.

nonNegotiables: Sparrow is the only temporarily supported wallet coordinator.
Unsupported wallet coordinators must not be introduced by surface-reduction work.
The custom wallet layer is removed from Bails so the supported runtime is installer-focused.
The Python Codex32 replacement is reviewed separately from the Bails installer.
Handoff uses fresh Tails and explicit user-selected paths rather than an indiscriminate persistent-state clone.
assumptions: The project intends to preserve a guided experience on a dedicated Tails USB.
No measured usability, performance, or user-success evidence was supplied.
No completed independent audit or mature project release-signing operation was supplied.

opportunities.title: Align claims with the supported trust boundary
opportunities.summary: Make promises derive from implemented controls, remove unfinished paths from supported use, and narrow the project-owned runtime.
opportunities.diagnosis: Security claims, feature status, and operational guidance are not governed by one explicit threat model and support matrix, while a broad local scripting layer owns security-sensitive transitions.

evidence.claim: The supplied review identifies overclaiming, single-maintainer trust, cloning, residual operational risks, audience mismatch, and maturity concerns.
Current user-facing documentation makes absolute privacy and security claims, presents unfinished cloning as available, and mixes implemented and planned behavior.
The advertised clone flow exits as coming soon, while existing issues and branches separately address unfinished actions, release authentication, tests, and wallet-surface reduction.
Without a single support boundary, documentation can drift into promising controls that the runtime does not own or implement.

desiredInvariants: Every privacy or security claim maps to an implemented control and names its residual risks.
Planned features are never presented as current supported behavior.
Unsupported or untested actions are absent from primary installation and menu paths.
Every executed CipherStick update is authenticated before execution.
The supported wallet coordinator set is explicit and limited to Sparrow.
Every optional handoff path is selected explicitly by the person performing the transfer.
Bails never silently includes or excludes wallet ciphertext or identifying persistent state.
Maturity, review status, user assumptions, and non-goals appear before installation instructions.

options.title: Calibrate documentation around the current implementation
options.summary: Replace guarantees with bounded properties, publish limitations, separate planned features, and replace unfinished cloning claims with a fresh-Tails handoff design.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: The documentation changes directly address overclaiming, threat-model visibility, unfinished cloning promotion, audience expectations, and maturity disclosure, but do not reduce runtime code risk.
The affected user-facing text is the direct subject of this option.
Replacing the unfinished full-state clone with a fresh-Tails, user-controlled handoff prevents reliance on the absent implementation and avoids silent state transfer.
A support matrix and threat model make future documentation drift more visible but rely on ongoing review discipline.

tradeoffs.assessment: Bounded claims reduce unsafe reliance outside implemented controls, while runtime vulnerabilities remain unchanged.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Map every surviving claim to source and residual-risk documentation.

tradeoffs.assessment: Documentation and menu exposure changes add no runtime work.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Confirm no executable path changed in the documentation-only commits.

tradeoffs.assessment: No process or retained data changes are introduced.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Confirm the change set contains no runtime modifications.

tradeoffs.assessment: Removing unsupported actions from primary paths reduces predictable dead-end workflows without changing supported operations.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inspect all menus and setup guides for links to unsupported actions.

tradeoffs.assessment: The immediate workload is small, but every future claim needs support-matrix review.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Add a documentation review item to the release checklist and observe review burden for two releases.

tradeoffs.assessment: No supported data or executable interface changes.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Confirm installation instructions retain the current supported path.

residualRisks: The project-owned runtime remains broad and insufficiently tested.
Mutable project updates remain unsafe until the existing release-authentication issue is completed.
Claims can drift again without release discipline.

workPackages: Publish the threat model and support matrix.
Hide the unfinished clone command and document fresh-Tails handoff with explicit optional transfer paths.
acceptanceCriteria: Every user-facing security claim names an implemented property and limitation.
Current and planned features are visibly separated.
Primary installation and menu paths do not expose the unfinished clone command.
Handoff documentation separates Tails installation, authenticated Bails archive transfer, and user-selected optional data.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Revert each focused documentation or menu change independently.

options.title: Narrow and authenticate the supported runtime
options.summary: Include calibrated documentation, remove custom wallet logic, keep Sparrow only, authenticate releases, replace full-state cloning with explicit fresh-Tails handoff, and add regression tests.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: This option addresses the strongest claims, trust-surface, handoff, user-expectation, and maturity concerns while preserving guided setup.
Documentation calibration and removal of unsupported paths directly resolve the observed source/document mismatch.
Existing focused work can hide unfinished actions, authenticate releases, establish tests, and remove custom wallet code.
Narrow component ownership plus a support matrix reduces drift, though governance discipline remains necessary.

tradeoffs.assessment: Removing local wallet logic, authenticating updates, and replacing undefined clone flows with explicit handoff choices narrow project-owned attack paths; inherited upstream and user risks remain.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run focused security regression cases for release verification, unsupported actions, and coordinator scope.

tradeoffs.assessment: Fewer bundled components may reduce setup work, but Bitcoin Core IBD still dominates and no measurement exists.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure setup wall time separately from IBD on representative supported USB hardware before and after.

tradeoffs.assessment: Removing bundled Python wallet code may reduce disk and occasional process use, but Bitcoin Core and Sparrow dominate resource consumption.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare persistent-storage size and peak RSS for the supported flow.

tradeoffs.assessment: Fewer supported flows and regression coverage reduce drift and dead ends, while depending on Sparrow adds an upstream compatibility boundary.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise clean install, restart, update failure, Core verification, Sparrow launch, and unsupported-action cases.

tradeoffs.assessment: Release signing, key rotation, CI triage, and Sparrow compatibility become explicit maintainer duties.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Dry-run one signed release and key-recovery exercise; record maintenance time for two releases.

tradeoffs.assessment: Existing custom-wallet users need clear compatibility and recovery guidance, and PR 202 must be split to avoid adding unsupported coordinators.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inventory persisted wallet formats and test documented recovery before removing local wallet code.

residualRisks: CipherStick scripts still run inside the user's Tails session and configure Persistent Storage.
Hardware, firmware, physical compromise, coercion, endpoint correlation, and secret loss remain outside project control.
Sparrow introduces its own upstream supply-chain and compatibility assumptions.

workPackages: Land bounded claims, project-specific threat model, and fresh-Tails handoff documentation as separate reviews.
Hide unfinished actions using the existing focused branch.
Split and rebase PR 202 to remove bails-wallet without adding Bisq, Liana, Wasabi, or generic coordinator support.
Review the Python Codex32 replacement separately from the Bails installer.
Complete authenticated release updates and the functional test harness.
acceptanceCriteria: Only implemented and tested features appear in supported paths.
Sparrow is the sole named supported coordinator.
Functional tests exercise the security-critical supported flow.
Fresh-Tails handoff authenticates the Bails archive and requires explicit choices for optional data.
migrationNotes: Document recovery for any wallet material created by the removed local wallet flow.
Do not merge coordinator additions bundled into the current PR 202 branch.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Revert each focused branch independently; keep unsupported actions hidden during rollback.

options.title: Replace the runtime with an upstream-only guide
options.summary: Remove CipherStick executable code and maintain guidance for experienced users of official Tails and Bitcoin Core tooling.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Removing project runtime directly reduces single-project executable trust but does not remove upstream, host, operational, or user-error risks.
A documentation-only project cannot present absent runtime features as implemented, though documentation can still overclaim.
Unfinished project actions disappear with the runtime.
Project-owned control drift is minimized, while users assume the integration decisions and error surface.

tradeoffs.assessment: Project-specific execution paths disappear, but manual integration errors and direct upstream-verification duties shift to each user.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare threat-model coverage and observed setup errors in guided user studies for automated and manual flows.

tradeoffs.assessment: Resulting performance depends on each user's choices; IBD remains dominant.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure complete manual setups on the same supported hardware used for the automated baseline.

tradeoffs.assessment: The final Tails, Bitcoin Core, and coordinator workloads remain, with only the project helper footprint removed.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare persistent-storage and peak-RSS measurements for equivalent final configurations.

tradeoffs.assessment: Fewer local scripts remove their failure modes, but installation and recovery outcomes become more dependent on user execution and documentation freshness.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run observed setup and recovery studies against pinned upstream versions.

tradeoffs.assessment: Release signing and runtime CI duties disappear, while upstream documentation tracking and user support remain.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Estimate update-review effort across two upstream release cycles.

tradeoffs.assessment: This abandons the guided product and changes the intended audience; existing users still need recovery and transition guidance.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inventory existing persisted state and validate a no-CipherStick recovery guide before retiring releases.

residualRisks: Manual verification and persistence errors may compromise security or availability.
Upstream hardware, firmware, Tor, endpoint, physical, and secret-loss risks remain.
Documentation can still become stale or make unsupported claims.

workPackages: Document recovery and transition for existing users.
Replace project instructions with versioned upstream guidance.
Archive executable releases after a defined support period.
acceptanceCriteria: Users can recover existing data without project executables.
Every step links to authenticated upstream artifacts and official guidance.
The project no longer distributes executable installation or wallet code.
migrationNotes: This is a product retirement, not a drop-in refactor.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Restore a supported signed release and its maintenance obligations.

opportunities.recommendation: Retain a guided product only under a narrower authenticated and tested boundary; choose the upstream-only guide if the project cannot sustain release and review operations.

openQuestions: What release-signing and key-rotation process can maintainers operate?
What independent review threshold is required before leaving alpha?
What interface, if any, should present optional handoff paths without deciding for the user?
